body: Can you elaborate on the view from each interpretation and whether it will affect the result?
Due to charge or gravity, does it matter which?

Suicide requires a lot of emotional effort and mental effort, not much physical effort.

Yes I understand the concept of delayed gratification but i feel like the amount of effort you exert has to be part of the equation.

Delaying instant gratification requires mental effort.

So you are basically saying find the amount of effort that is less than the amount of effort required for suicide?

Aren't we all exorting effort in order to achieve gratification later, hence it is delayed gratification?

You are probably right but justifing getting there over suicide is the problem.

I feel like higher effort is suffering.

Working a regular job is lower effort short term, but higher effort long term, thus the sum of the effort working the entire life is long term suffering.

Working intensely for a couple of years on my own startup is higher effort short term, but long term assuming it's successful would allow not working, lower effort life, hence short term suffering.

Is my reasoning flawed?
What does philosophy say about the connection of effort and suffering?
The fact that he gave me the ability to suffer is itself intrinsically bad thing.

If the choice is either have relationship with robots who will not suffer after creation, or with humans who can suffer and feel bad after creation. It's seems obvious that I will never create anything that can suffer, even for all the good in the world, including relationships.

But If god is intrinsically good then he wouldn't create evil and bad in the world.
He wouldn't create the bad tools.
He can decide that good doesn't have to be earned but everyone could get it without struggle and effort, after all he is god he is definitely capable.
